title: App Builder Project Summary
description: What the service says about a project over its own boundary. It is a projection, not the project: the manifest, knowledge pack and intake bundle are large artifacts with their own contracts and are referenced by identity here rather than inlined. This is a contract family because the Console was carrying a hand-written copy of it, and the two most recent additions — the lifecycle claim and the build identity — were typed twice by hand with nothing checking that the two spellings agreed.

state.description: Legacy build progress. `generated` means a directory exists and `verified` means a build once succeeded under a resolution nobody recorded; neither is a readiness verdict. `lifecycle` is the canonical claim.

lifecycle.description: Where this project stands on the one readiness ladder, and why. Null for a project carrying no exact artifact identity for a lifecycle to be about — which is most of them, and is the honest answer rather than a gap.

basis.description: One sentence a person can check against the evidence. A projection that states a position without saying why is one nobody can dispute.

missing.description: What this project would have to record to go further.

anyOf.description: What the last verification installed from, ran under and built. Recording is unconditional; claiming is not, which is what `reproducible` separates.

npm.description: Null when npm could not be asked. An npm nobody could read is unknown, never assumed to be the declared one.

reproducible.description: False when the build ran under anything other than the declared toolchain. The record is still complete; it simply is not a reproducibility claim.

approvedIntakeBundleId.description: That this project can be rerun without re-keying the questionnaire. The bundle itself is a large artifact and is fetched separately.
